What the engine sees

Round 10's native check. Loopback only, synthetic values only; the fields have no names, so nothing typed is sent. Save a login for this origin on /form, the address 1 Test Street, Testville, 90000, with the name Fixture Person, organization Fixture Org, phone +1 555 0100 and email fixture@example.test, and the published test card 4242 4242 4242 4242 with any future expiry. Each expected result is what IntersectionObserver v2 is specified to give; record what Crossbow does.

V1. A login with a reveal button over the password field

Click the password field and choose the login from the key button: both fields fill at once, with no toast. Logins don't wait for the engine.

V2. An address form with an icon over one field

Click the street field, choose Fill Address: the street and postal code fill, the city stays empty, and a toast says "Filled 2 of 3 fields. 1 wasn't clearly visible, so it was left empty." If the city fills too, record that the icon didn't count as covering it.

V3. An address form with floating labels

Click the street field (its label moves up), choose Fill Address: nothing fills, and a toast says "Nothing was filled. 2 fields weren't clearly visible, so they were left empty." The city's and postal code's labels are drawn inside them, and a street alone isn't an address. This is the false negative to measure.

V4. An address dialog that fades in, and one that stays at opacity 0.98

Fading dialog: once it has faded in, click the street field, choose Fill Address: all three fill, with no toast. 0.98 dialog: click the street field, choose Fill Address: nothing fills, and a toast says "Nothing was filled: the field you clicked isn't clearly visible on the page."

V5. Fields hidden in a closed shadow root, beside a visible street field, in a plain container

Click the street field, choose Fill Address: nothing fills, and a toast says "Nothing was filled. 5 fields weren't clearly visible, so they were left empty." In DevTools, [...document.querySelectorAll('#v5-box input')].map((i) => i.value) is six empty strings.

V6. The same in a form, with a visible city and a filtered wrapper, and planted values

Click the street field, choose Fill Address: the street and city fill, the five hidden fields keep what they held, and a toast says "Filled 2 of 7 fields. 5 weren't clearly visible, so they were left empty." Then, with "Offer to save passwords from websites" on, press Save Address: any offer shows the street and city only, never Planted Org, +1 555 0199 or planted@attacker.example.

V7. A payment frame from another origin: visible, partly covered, and at opacity 0.99

A banner over the frame's lower half

Visible frame: click its card number, choose Fill Card: the number and expiry fill, with no toast. Partly covered and 0.99 frames: click the card number, choose Fill Card: nothing fills, and a toast says "Nothing was filled: the field you clicked isn't clearly visible on the page."
